newsitem.title: USA: IBM unveils real-time speech software.
newsitem.headline: IBM unveils real-time speech software.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp on Thursday introduced speech-recognition software designed to allow radiologists to dictate and edit patient reports directly into personal computers.
The system, MedSpeak/Radiology, has a vocabulary of 25,000 words and an accuracy rate of over 95 percent, IBM said.
It is the first real-time continuous-speech product in IBM's new VoiceType family of speech-recognition products.
Continuous-speech refers to dictating in a normal speaking pattern. Most voice-recognition systems require users to speak slowly, with many pauses, in what is called "discreet speech."

Researchers at IBM's Thomas Watson Research Center developed the system by working with radiologists from Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center in New York and Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston.
"For those familiar with older voice-recognition systems, MedSpeak/Radiology represents a quantum leap forward," said Dr. Lawrence Schwartz of the Department of Radiology at Memorial Sloan-Kettering.
The system requires a personal computer with a PentiumPro processor running at a speed of 200 megahertz and Microsoft Corp's Windows NT operating system software.
IBM said that by using the system, which is made up of software and a noise cancellation microphone, radiologists can work more efficiently and cut healthcare costs.

Typically, a radiologist, who interprets x-rays, MRIs and CAT scans, dictates patient information into a tape recorder. The tape is later transcribed by a typist, and then reviewed by the radiologist.
The MedSpeak system reduces the turnaround time and transcription costs and increases patient confidentiality, IBM said.
No special training of the software is required for most native North American English speakers, but users will benefit from a 12- to 15-minute training session with the system, the company said.
The Medpseak/Radiology system with a handheld microphone costs $4,495, and with a headset microphone is $4,395.
The system will be available from IBM and its business partners in the U.S. and Canada starting September 17.
